hha.q: The curriculum lists risk factors that compromise healthy skin. Which group is correct?
choices: Immobility, poor nutrition, moisture and illness
Reading and watching television
Drinking too much water
Having visitors
hha.exp: Risk factors: immobility, poor nutrition, illness, moisture-related problems, circulatory problems and pressure. Preventive measures include position changes, skin care, keeping skin clean and dry, and good nutrition (Module XII, Unit B, Integumentary).

hha.q: Which rule of proper body mechanics does the curriculum teach?
choices: Bend at the waist with straight legs
Twist at the waist to turn
Bend at the knees and hips, keep objects close to the body, use a wide base of support and turn with the feet
Lift with the arms only
hha.exp: Body mechanics rules (Procedure XII-2): firm/wide base of support, back straight, face the direction of movement, one foot ahead of the other, keep objects close, use body weight when pushing/pulling, bend at knees and hips, turn with feet and do not twist.

hha.q: Which body position does the curriculum call 'Fowler's position'?
choices: Lying flat on the back
Lying on the stomach
Sitting up in bed with the head of the bed raised
Lying on the side
hha.exp: Basic positions: Fowler's (head of bed raised, semi-sitting), supine (on the back), prone (on the stomach) and lateral (on the side). Fowler's helps breathing and eating (Module XII, Unit B, Musculoskeletal, Lesson 1b).

hha.q: Before transferring a client from the bed to a wheelchair (Procedure XII-26), the worker must:
choices: Leave the brakes off so the chair can be adjusted
Angle the wheelchair next to the bed and lock the brakes
Place the wheelchair across the room
Ask the client to jump into the chair
hha.exp: Procedure XII-26: explain, wash hands, angle the wheelchair next to the bed, lock brakes, use a safety belt if needed, dangle legs, stand the client, rotate until the back faces the chair, back up until the chair touches the legs, lower the client, adjust footrests.

hha.q: When helping a client to stand from the edge of the bed (Procedure XII-25), the worker should:
choices: Pull the client up by the arms
Place one foot between the client's feet, brace a weak knee, hold the client around the waist, and lift on the count of three by rocking weight to the back foot
Stand behind the client
Let the client hold the worker's neck
hha.exp: Procedure XII-25: bed in lowest position; one foot forward between the client's feet; brace a weak knee; client puts strongest foot under self; both arms around the client's waist; on 'one-two-three' the client pushes down and leans forward while the worker rocks weight to the back foot and lifts; support until the client stands safely.

hha.q: When helping a client walk (Procedure XII-14), on which side should the worker stand?
choices: The client's strong side
The client's weak side
Directly in front
Directly behind
hha.exp: Procedure XII-14 (Helping the Client to Walk): reassure, advise proper shoes, practice standing and shifting weight, walk slowly with small steps, walk on the client's weak side using correct positioning, short distances, observe and report.

hha.q: Why does the curriculum say ambulation (walking) is important for the client?
choices: It gives the worker a break
It increases self-esteem, promotes circulation, strengthens joints and muscles, and prevents atrophy and contractures
It is required by insurance
It replaces the need for meals
hha.exp: Importance of ambulation: increases self-esteem and well-being, promotes circulation, strengthens joints and muscles, prevents atrophy and contractures (complications of immobility). Devices: cane, walker, crutches (Module XII, Unit B, Lesson 2 Ambulation).

hha.q: What is the difference between active and passive range of motion exercises, as taught in the curriculum?
choices: Active is done in the morning; passive at night
Active: the client moves the joint alone; passive: the worker moves the client's limb through the motion
Active uses weights; passive uses water
There is no difference
hha.exp: Active ROM: the client moves the joints independently. Passive ROM: the caregiver moves the limbs through their range. Resistive ROM: movement against resistance. ROM prevents disuse syndrome, atrophy and contractures (Module XII, Unit B, Lesson 3).

hha.q: During a bed bath (Procedure XII-5), in what order should the body be washed?
choices: Feet first, then upward
From head to toe, cleanest to least clean, with genitals and buttocks last
Genitals first for hygiene
Any order the worker prefers
hha.exp: Procedure XII-5 (Bed Bath): provide privacy and warmth, test water temperature, form a mitt with the washcloth, wash and dry from head to toe and cleanest to least clean, one part at a time, keep exposure minimal, change water when needed, wash genitals and buttocks last, let the client participate.

hha.q: While bathing, which changes does the curriculum say must be observed and reported?
choices: Only the amount of soap used
Skin changes, dizziness or weakness, mental status changes, and refusal of service
Whether the client sang
The brand of shampoo
hha.exp: Safety during bathing: regulate water temperature, check environmental and equipment safety, and observe for physical and emotional changes: skin changes, dizziness/weakness, mental status changes and refusal of service, and report to the supervisor (Module XII, Unit B, Bathing).

hha.q: Before a tub or shower bath (Procedure XII-3), the worker should:
choices: Fill the tub with very hot water to warm the bathroom
Ensure warmth in the bathroom, remove loose rugs, check safety devices, place rubber mats and a chair, and test the water temperature
Leave the client alone to undress and get in
Use the client's bathroom without checking it
hha.exp: Procedure XII-3: explain, wash hands, assemble equipment, ensure warmth, remove loose rugs, check safety devices, place rubber mats and chairs, test water temperature, assist in and out, drain and clean, wash hands, observe and report.

hha.q: When providing hair care, the curriculum says to:
choices: Use any brush available in the house
Use the client's own brush or comb, follow their preferences, and report sores, crusts, dandruff or hair loss
Cut the hair short to make care easier
Skip hair care if the client is in bed
hha.exp: Hair care: seek information about the client's hairstyle preferences and routines, use the client's own brush or comb (infection control), promote self-care, shampoo when appropriate (Procedure XII-6, Shampoo in Bed), and report sores, crusts, dandruff or hair loss.

hha.q: Which mouth conditions must be reported to the supervisor, according to the curriculum?
choices: Fresh breath after brushing
Cracked bleeding lips, sores, swollen or bleeding gums, white or discolored patches, loose teeth, excess drooling or difficulty swallowing
That the client prefers mint toothpaste
That the client has dentures
hha.exp: Report: cracked, bleeding or dry lips; sores/lesions; swollen, bleeding or reddened tongue or gums; white, brown or discolored patches; loose teeth or worn surfaces; decreased or excess saliva or drooling; difficulty swallowing; pain in mouth, teeth, throat or ear (Module XII, Unit B, Mouth Care).

hha.q: When cleaning dentures, the curriculum says to:
choices: Hold them over an empty sink
Line the sink with a washcloth and add water so they are protected if dropped, then store them in a denture cup covered with water when not in use
Boil them to sterilize
Leave them to dry on the table overnight
hha.exp: Denture care: remove with a gloved hand (rock gently; pull down for uppers, up for lowers), place in a denture cup immediately, cushion the sink with a washcloth and water, brush with toothpaste then denture cleaner, insert top first, store in water when not in use (Module XII, Unit B, Mouth Care b; Procedure XII-10).

hha.q: For a client who is edentulous (has no teeth), how does the curriculum say to clean the mouth?
choices: Use a hard toothbrush with lots of toothpaste
Clean and massage the mouth and gums with a lemon-glycerin swab or a moistened toothette
Skip mouth care since there are no teeth
Use mouthwash only
hha.exp: Edentulous mouth care: clean and massage the mouth and gums with a lemon glycerin swab or moistened toothette (Module XII, Unit B, Mouth Care c; Procedure XII-10). Mouth care is still needed when there are no teeth.

hha.q: When shaving a client with a safety razor (Procedure XII-9), the worker should:
choices: Shave against the grain with long strokes
Wash hands, put on gloves, pull the skin tight, shave with gentle short strokes in the same direction, rinse the razor often, and report any irritation or redness
Shave dry to save time
Use the same razor for several clients
hha.exp: Procedure XII-9: explain, wash hands, gloves, towel under chin, wash face and leave wet, apply shaving cream, pull skin tight, gentle short strokes in the same direction, rinse razor often, rinse and pat dry, after-shave, report skin irritation, redness or scaling. Standard Precautions apply.

hha.q: According to the curriculum, what may the home care worker do to a client's fingernails and toenails?
choices: Cut and trim them with clippers
File them only; cutting or trimming is not permitted, and the care plan should be discussed with the RN
Remove ingrown nails
Apply medicated treatments
hha.exp: Do not cut or trim fingernails or toenails. Nails may only be filed; discuss the plan of care with the RN. Soak, clean under nails, push back cuticles, file, apply lotion, and report pain, redness, open areas, dry scaly skin or cracked nails (Module XII, Unit B, Lessons 4-5; Procedure XII-8).

hha.q: For a client with a weak or paralyzed side, the curriculum teaches to:
choices: Dress the strong side first and undress the weak side first
Dress the weak side first and undress from the strong side first
Always dress both arms at once
Avoid dressing the weak side
hha.exp: Assist with shirt/pants on the weak side first; remove from the strong side first. Let the client choose clothing, encourage self-dressing, assist when the client asks or shows fatigue, and use adaptive clothing when in the care plan (Module XII, Unit B, Dressing; Procedure XII-12).

hha.q: Before applying elastic support stockings (Procedure XII-13) to a client who has been up and about, the worker should:
choices: Apply them immediately while the client stands
Have the client lie down with legs elevated for 15 minutes, make sure legs are clean and dry, then apply smoothly with no wrinkles and the heel in place
Apply them over wet lotion
Apply them only at night
hha.exp: Procedure XII-13: if the client has been up, lie down with legs elevated 15 minutes first; legs clean and dry; apply smoothly with no wrinkles, heel in the heel of the stocking; relieve toe pressure; remove at least once daily per care plan; observe and report changes in skin color, temperature, swelling or sores.

hha.q: When making an occupied bed (Procedure XII-16), how is the soiled bottom sheet handled?
choices: Pulled out from under the client in one motion
Rolled up to and under the client's back, the clean sheet placed and folded next to it, then the client is turned to the clean side
Left in place and covered with a clean sheet
Shaken out in the room
hha.exp: Procedure XII-16: turn the client onto the side, roll the soiled bottom sheet up to and under the client, smooth the mattress, position the clean sheet and fold it under the soiled one, tuck and miter, turn the client to the clean side, remove soiled linen from the other side, finish tucking, change pillowcases.

hha.q: When picking up an infant (Procedure XII-35), the worker should:
choices: Lift under the arms
Put one hand under the buttocks and the other under the head, neck and shoulders
Lift by the hands
Lift by the feet
hha.exp: Procedure XII-35 (Handling the Infant): wash hands, one hand under the buttocks, the other under the head, neck and shoulders; support head, neck and buttocks in the 'football' hold. Conserve body heat, position and transport safely (Module XII, Unit C).

hha.q: According to the curriculum, when may the home care worker be asked to give personal care to a well baby?
choices: Whenever the parents want to go out
When no other caretaker is available and the mother is unavailable
Only in hospitals
Never
hha.exp: Well-baby personal care is needed when no other caretaker is available and the mother is unavailable. The worker respects cultural, religious and social diversity in childcare, follows the care plan and reports concerns to the RN supervisor (Module XII, Unit C).

hha.q: The curriculum says that if the worker is unfamiliar with a piece of special equipment in the client's home, the worker should:
choices: Try it out carefully on the client
Not use it; request instruction and demonstration from the supervisor, nurse or therapist
Ask the client's grandchild to show them
Look it up online during the visit
hha.exp: Worker's role: check the plan of care, read operating instructions, do NOT use equipment you are unfamiliar with (request instruction and demonstration), encourage client independence, change or charge batteries, maintain and store equipment, observe its state of repair and client problems, record and report (Module XII, Unit D).

hha.q: When using a hydraulic (Hoyer) lift (Procedure XII-37), what must the worker do after lifting the client a few inches and before moving the lift?
choices: Release the valve quickly
Check all connections to make sure they are fastened tightly and working properly
Remove the sling
Ask the client to hold the chains
hha.exp: Procedure XII-37: check the valves, clear the floor, open the lift legs to the widest position, lock the wheelchair and bed, position the sling midway between head and thigh, attach chains (longer to thigh, shorter to head), tell the client before pumping, and after lifting a few inches check all connections before moving.

hha.q: In a slide board transfer (Procedure XII-38), the wheelchair should be placed:
choices: Facing the bed, two feet away
At a 45-degree angle to the bed with brakes locked and armrest removed if possible
Behind the client
Across the room
hha.exp: Procedure XII-38: wheelchair at a 45-degree angle, brakes locked, armrest removed if able; cover the board with a pillowcase if the client is unclothed; client leans away while the board is placed under the buttocks; transfer toward the strong side; client does small push-ups across the board; gait belt as necessary.

hha.q: What are the 'Five Medication Rights' listed in the curriculum?
choices: Right price, right pharmacy, right brand, right color, right bottle
Right person, right medication, right dose, right time, right route
Right doctor, right nurse, right aide, right family, right agency
Right morning, right noon, right evening, right night, right week
hha.exp: The Five Medication Rights: right person, right medication, right dose, right time, right route (Procedures XII-39 to XII-43). The worker checks each against the label and the care plan.

hha.q: What is the difference between 'administering' medication and 'assisting with self-administration', according to the curriculum?
choices: There is no difference

Assisting means reminding, bringing the medication and equipment, reading the label, positioning the client and opening the container so the client takes it themselves; administering (giving the drug) is NOT the worker's role
Assisting means choosing the dose
Administering is allowed when the family agrees
hha.exp: The home care worker assists with self-administration: reminds the client of the time, brings the medication and equipment, reads or shows the label, positions the client, opens the container, provides liquids, stores medication properly, cleans equipment and washes hands. The worker does not administer medication (Module XII, Unit E).

hha.q: A client has trouble swallowing a pill and asks the worker to crush it into applesauce. According to the curriculum, the worker should:
choices: Crush it; applesauce is harmless
Not crush or add medication to food; follow the plan of care and report the swallowing difficulty
Dissolve it in juice instead
Skip the dose
hha.exp: Do not crush or add medications to other food such as applesauce or ice cream. If a nurse or family member pre-pours medication, follow the plan of care. Report when the client does not take medication or takes it improperly (Module XII, Unit E).

hha.q: While checking the 'right medication' (Procedure XII-40), the worker sees the name on the bottle does not match the care plan. The worker should:
choices: Give it anyway because the doctor must have changed it
Not give it; contact the supervisor for instructions, explain to the client, and record and report the problem
Give half the dose to be safe
Throw the bottle away
hha.exp: Procedures XII-39 to XII-43: wash hands, read the label, check the expiration date, compare the name/medication/dose/time/route with the care plan. If they match, assist as ordered; if not, contact the supervisor, explain to the client, and record and report.

hha.q: Which situation does the curriculum say must be recorded and reported IMMEDIATELY when assisting with medication?
choices: The client took the medication on time
The client takes supplements or herbs not ordered by the physician, or has an unusual reaction
The pharmacy bag was blue
The client drank water with the pill
hha.exp: Record and report immediately if the client does not take medication or takes it improperly, takes medications/supplements/herbs not ordered by the physician, has an unusual reaction, or if medications are dropped or mixed up (Module XII, Unit E).

hha.q: Before assisting with a medication, Procedure XII-40 says to check what on the label besides the medication name?
choices: The price
The expiration date
The pharmacist's name
The color of the pill
hha.exp: Basic assistance skills: Standard Precautions, reading labels and checking the expiration date, checking the Five Rights, proper storage and disposal (Module XII, Unit E; Procedure XII-40).

hha.q: To measure a client's fluid intake (Procedure XII-32), the curriculum says to:
choices: Estimate by eye at the end of the day
Measure each serving container's capacity ahead of time, write down what was served, measure what is left, and subtract to get the total consumed
Count the number of cups only
Ask the family at the end of the week
hha.exp: Procedure XII-32: get the client's cooperation; measure each serving container in advance with a measuring cup and keep the list; record types and amounts served; measure leftovers; subtract leftover from served and add totals; record total intake for the period.

hha.q: When measuring urinary output (Procedure XII-33), which observations must be reported?
choices: Normal pale yellow urine
Strong-smelling or cloudy urine, blood in the urine, a very small amount, or pain or difficulty passing urine
That the client used the commode
The time of day only
hha.exp: Procedure XII-33: pour urine into a measuring pitcher on a flat surface, record the amount, discard unless a specimen is needed, clean equipment, wash hands, and report strong-smelling or cloudy urine, blood, very small amounts, or pain or difficulty passing urine.

hha.q: When assisting with changing a clean dressing (Procedure XII-34), what does the worker do after removing the old dressing and gloves?
choices: Immediately apply the new dressing with the same gloves
Wash hands and put on new gloves before cleaning the skin and applying the new dressing
Leave the wound open to the air
Call the family to finish
hha.exp: Procedure XII-34 (using Standard Precautions): place a waste bag near the client, put on gloves, remove and discard the old dressing and gloves, wash hands, put on new gloves, clean the skin per the care plan, apply and tape the new dressing, discard waste, wash hands, report changes in the wound's appearance.

hha.q: After applying a condom catheter (Procedure XII-19), the worker checks that:
choices: The tubing is taped tightly around the thigh
The tubing is one to two inches below the tip of the penis and the tip of the condom is not twisted
The condom is rolled up to the abdomen
The bag is above the level of the bladder
hha.exp: Procedure XII-19: expose only the genital area, wash and dry the penis, observe skin for sores, attach condom to tubing, roll on as directed by the care plan, check tubing is 1–2 inches below the tip and not twisted, record application and report any sores or raw areas.

hha.q: When cleaning the skin and catheter tubing (Procedure XII-20), the worker should:
choices: Pull on the catheter to clean under it
Hold the catheter with one hand while wiping with the other, never pull, clean the tubing starting nearest the client, and position so the tubing has no kinks or pulling
Disconnect the tubing to clean it
Clean from the bag toward the client
hha.exp: Procedure XII-20: wash the genital area gently with soap and water, do not pull on the catheter (hold with one hand, wipe with the other), push back foreskin on an uncircumcised male, observe for sores, crusting, leakage or bleeding, clean tubing starting nearest the client, keep tubing free of kinks, tape as directed, record the time.

hha.q: After helping a client sit up in bed (Procedure XII-23), what must the worker check before continuing?
choices: Whether the TV is on
Whether the client is dizzy or weak
Whether the window is open
Whether the pillow matches the sheets
hha.exp: Procedure XII-23: face the head of the bed with the outer foot forward, raise the head of the bed or lock arms with the client, have the client bend knees, pull to sitting by rocking, place pillows, and check the client for dizziness or weakness before continuing.

hha.q: When positioning a client on the side (Procedure XII-22), where does the curriculum say to place pillows or folded towels?
choices: Only under the head
Under the head and neck, at the back, under the top leg and foot, and under the top arm
Under both feet only
Between the knees only
hha.exp: Procedure XII-22, client on side: center the client, turn onto the side, align the body, place pillows under head and neck, at the back, under the top leg and foot, and under the top arm; position hips, legs, shoulders and arms; cover and make comfortable.

hha.q: Before transferring a client from wheelchair to toilet (Procedure XII-28), the worker should first:
choices: Remove the client's shoes
Check the bathroom for supports and grab bars, place the wheelchair facing the toilet, lock the wheels and raise the footrests
Turn off the bathroom light for privacy
Ask the client to stand alone
hha.exp: Procedure XII-28: check for supports and grab bars, place the wheelchair facing the toilet, lock wheels, raise footrests, assist to stand, rotate until the back is toward the toilet, arrange clothing, assist to sit, allow privacy, assist with cleaning, reverse the steps, assist with handwashing.

hha.q: Before shampooing a client's hair in bed (Procedure XII-6), the worker asks the client which products to use. Why?
choices: To save money
To prevent allergies or reactions
Because the agency requires a receipt
To choose the best smell
hha.exp: Procedure XII-6: assemble equipment and ask the client which products to use to prevent allergies or reactions; make a trough to keep the bed dry; check room temperature; protect eyes and ears while lathering from front to back; rinse thoroughly; dry hair; observe and report.

hha.q: When bathing an infant (Procedure XII-36), the worker washes the body:
choices: From the feet up
From head to foot, after shampooing, rinsing and drying the head first
Starting with the diaper area
In any order
hha.exp: Procedure XII-36: wash hands, assemble equipment, ensure room and water temperature, prepare the changing area, undress and cover the baby, lower into water, shampoo/rinse/dry the head, wash the body head to foot, wash genitals correctly, dry, lotion per care plan, diaper and dress, nail care if needed, observe and report.

hha.q: When making an unoccupied bed (Procedure XII-15), how is a clean pillowcase put on?
choices: Stuff the pillow in from the open end
Turn the soiled case inside out to remove it; grasp the clean case at the center of the bottom seam, fold it over the hand, grasp the pillow end through the case and pull the case over the pillow
Shake the pillow into the case
Pillowcases are not changed
hha.exp: Procedure XII-15: remove and fold bedding to re-use, smooth the mattress pad, position and tuck the bottom sheet with mitered corners, position top covers, add the spread, change the pillowcase using the fold-over-hand method, remove soiled linen, wash hands.

teas.q:
Read this passage: 'Handwashing is the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infection. Nurses, CNAs, and visitors should wash hands before and after patient contact. Proper technique includes 20 seconds of scrubbing with soap.'

What is the main idea?
choices: Visitors should wash their hands
Handwashing prevents the spread of infection
Scrubbing for 20 seconds is important
Soap is the best cleaning agent
teas.exp: The main idea is the central point of the passage. The first sentence states it directly: handwashing prevents infection. The other sentences are supporting details.

teas.q: Which of the following is a supporting detail (NOT the main idea) in this passage: 'Regular exercise has many benefits for seniors. It improves cardiovascular health, strengthens muscles, and reduces the risk of falls.'?
choices: Regular exercise has many benefits for seniors
Exercise improves cardiovascular health
Exercise is good for the elderly
Seniors need to be active
teas.exp: 'Improves cardiovascular health' is one specific benefit listed — a supporting detail. The main idea is that exercise has many benefits for seniors.

teas.q:
Read: 'While electronic health records (EHRs) have streamlined documentation, they also present challenges. Staff training requires time, system outages disrupt workflow, and privacy breaches are a growing concern.'

What is the author's main point?
choices: EHRs are dangerous
EHRs present challenges despite their benefits
All hospitals use EHRs
EHR training is too expensive
teas.exp: The passage acknowledges benefits ('streamlined documentation') while focusing on challenges. The main point is a balanced view: EHRs help but have problems.

teas.q: A pamphlet states: 'Get your flu shot today! It's free at your local pharmacy and takes only 10 minutes.' The author's purpose is to ___.
choices: Inform readers about flu symptoms
Entertain readers with health stories
Persuade readers to get vaccinated
Describe how vaccines are made
teas.exp: The call to action ('Get your flu shot today!') and persuasive tone indicate the purpose is to persuade. It is not informing (no data) or entertaining.

teas.q: A textbook chapter explains: 'The lymphatic system collects excess fluid from tissues and returns it to the bloodstream. It also plays a key role in immune defense.' This passage is primarily meant to ___.
choices: Persuade students to study lymph nodes
Entertain readers with biology trivia
Inform readers about lymphatic system functions
Argue that the lymphatic system is the most important system
teas.exp: A textbook explanation with factual, neutral language is meant to inform — to teach the reader about the topic.

teas.q: Read: 'Maria arrived at the nursing home at 6:45 AM, changed into her scrubs, checked the resident assignment board, and began her rounds.' What can you infer about Maria?
choices: Maria is a visitor
Maria is a patient
Maria works at the nursing home
Maria is a doctor
teas.exp: The details (scrubs, assignment board, rounds) strongly suggest Maria is a healthcare worker — most likely a CNA or nurse — not a visitor or patient.

teas.q: Read: 'The physician reviewed the chart, frowned, and immediately asked the nurse to increase the patient's oxygen flow rate.' What can you most likely infer?
choices: The patient is improving
The patient's oxygen levels may be too low
The physician is angry at the nurse
The chart was incorrectly filled out
teas.exp: Ordering increased oxygen flow suggests the doctor saw a sign of insufficient oxygenation (low SpO₂). The frown suggests concern, not anger.

teas.q: Read: 'Although the study showed promising results for the new antibiotic, the sample size was only 12 patients, and no control group was used.' What conclusion can best be drawn?
choices: The antibiotic is effective and ready for use
The results are unreliable due to methodological flaws
More antibiotics should be developed
The study proves the antibiotic works
teas.exp: Small sample + no control group = weak evidence. The study's design flaws mean the results cannot be trusted to show the antibiotic works.

teas.q: Which text structure is used when a passage describes a problem and then offers a solution?
choices: Cause and effect
Compare and contrast
Problem and solution
Chronological order
teas.exp: Problem-solution text presents an issue and then explains how it can be resolved. Example: 'Falls are common in nursing homes. To prevent them, bed alarms and non-slip socks are used.'

teas.q: A passage reads: 'Before the surgery, the patient was given general anesthesia. During the operation, the surgeon repaired the tendon. After recovery, physical therapy began.' This structure is ___.
choices: Problem-solution
Compare and contrast
Chronological order
Cause and effect
teas.exp: 'Before… During… After…' signals time order = chronological structure.

teas.q: Read: 'The patient was ambulatory, walking the hallway without assistance.' The word 'ambulatory' most nearly means ___.
choices: Confused
Able to walk
Attached to an IV
In pain
teas.exp: Context clue: 'walking the hallway without assistance' tells us ambulatory = able to walk independently.

teas.q: Read: 'The wound was benign — it showed no signs of infection.' The word 'benign' most nearly means ___.
choices: Dangerous
Harmless or not harmful
Infected
Deep
teas.exp: Context: 'no signs of infection' confirms benign = harmless. In oncology, benign means non-cancerous.

teas.q: Read: 'The physician noted that the patient's edema had worsened; her ankles were visibly swollen.' What does 'edema' mean?
choices: Skin infection
Swelling caused by fluid buildup
Muscle weakness
Allergic reaction
teas.exp: Context: 'ankles were visibly swollen' defines edema = fluid accumulation causing swelling.

teas.q: Read: 'Advance directives, such as a living will, allow patients to delineate their healthcare wishes before they become incapacitated.' The word 'delineate' most nearly means ___.
choices: Ignore
Specify or describe clearly
Argue about
Cancel
teas.exp: 'Allow patients to delineate their wishes' → delineate = to outline or describe clearly. Context: advance directives spell out wishes.

teas.q: Read: 'The empirical evidence from randomized controlled trials supersedes anecdotal reports in clinical decision-making.' The word 'supersedes' most nearly means ___.
choices: Supports
Replaces or takes priority over
Contradicts
Summarizes
teas.exp: 'Supersedes' = overrides, is more important than, takes precedence over. Empirical (scientific) evidence outranks anecdotes (personal stories).

teas.q:
Read: 'Pressure ulcers, often called bedsores, form when sustained pressure cuts off blood flow to skin. Stage I presents as redness; Stage II involves skin breakdown; Stages III and IV extend to deeper tissue and bone. Prevention through repositioning every 2 hours is far more effective than treatment.'

Which statement best summarizes this passage?
choices: Stage IV pressure ulcers extend to bone
Pressure ulcers develop progressively and are best prevented through repositioning
Bedsores are caused by poor hygiene
CNAs should report all red skin immediately
teas.exp: The passage covers: cause, stages, and prevention. The summary must capture all three. Option B does this — cause (pressure), progression (stages), and prevention (repositioning).

teas.q: What is 15 + 27?
teas.exp: 15 + 27 = 42. Basic addition is tested to build confidence before harder topics.

teas.q: Which of the following is an even number?
teas.exp: Even numbers are divisible by 2. 36 ÷ 2 = 18. All others (17, 23, 51) are odd.

teas.q: What is the value of |-8|?
teas.exp: Absolute value is the distance from zero on the number line — always positive. |-8| = 8.

teas.q: Order of operations: What is 2 + 3 × 4?
teas.exp: PEMDAS: Multiply before adding. 3 × 4 = 12, then 2 + 12 = 14.

teas.q: Which of the following is a prime number?
teas.exp: A prime number has exactly 2 factors: 1 and itself. 17 is prime. 1 has only 1 factor; 9 = 3×3; 21 = 3×7.

teas.q: What is 1/2 as a decimal?
What is 25% of 80?
What is 3/4 + 1/8?
teas.exp: Convert 3/4 to 6/8, then 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8. Always find a common denominator before adding fractions.

teas.q: A resident ate 3/5 of their meal. What percentage of the meal did they eat?
teas.exp: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.60 = 60%. This is both a math concept and a real CNA task — documenting meal intake as a percentage.

teas.q: A medication dose is 0.5 mg. If the available tablet is 0.25 mg, how many tablets are needed?
teas.exp: 0.5 ÷ 0.25 = 2 tablets. Desired dose ÷ dose on hand = number of tablets needed.

teas.q: Simplify the ratio 8:12.
teas.exp: Divide both by the GCF (4): 8÷4=2, 12÷4=3. Simplified ratio is 2:3.

teas.q: If 3 nurses care for 12 patients, how many nurses are needed for 20 patients (same ratio)?
teas.exp: Ratio: 3/12 = 1/4 (1 nurse per 4 patients). 20 ÷ 4 = 5 nurses.

teas.q: A solution is prepared with 20 mL of medicine in 80 mL of water. What is the concentration of medicine as a percentage?
teas.exp: Total solution = 20+80 = 100 mL. Medicine = 20 mL. 20/100 = 20%.

teas.q: Solve for x: x + 7 = 15
teas.exp: Subtract 7 from both sides: x = 15 - 7 = 8.

teas.q: Solve for x: 3x - 6 = 9
Which equation represents 'twice a number decreased by 5 equals 11'?
teas.exp: 'Twice a number' = 2n. 'Decreased by 5' = −5. 'Equals 11' = =11. So: 2n − 5 = 11.

teas.q: If f(x) = 2x² − 3, what is f(4)?
How many centimeters are in 1 meter?
teas.exp: 1 meter = 100 centimeters. The prefix 'centi-' means 1/100.

teas.q: A patient drinks 240 mL of juice. How many liters is that?
A patient's temperature is 100.4°F. Which of the following is the equivalent in Celsius? (Formula: C = (F−32) × 5/9)
Five patients had blood pressure readings: 120, 130, 125, 140, 130. What is the mode?
teas.exp: The mode is the value that appears most often. 130 appears twice; all others appear once.

teas.q: A bar graph shows facility falls: Jan=4, Feb=7, Mar=3, Apr=5. What is the mean number of falls per month?
A line graph shows patient weight (lbs) over 4 weeks: 180, 177, 175, 172. What is the average weekly weight loss?
choices: 2 lbs
2.67 lbs
3 lbs
8 lbs
teas.exp: Total loss = 180−172 = 8 lbs over 3 intervals (weeks 1→2, 2→3, 3→4). 8 ÷ 3 ≈ 2.67 lbs/week. Wait — 3 weeks between 4 readings. Answer is 2.67.

teas.q: A nurse has a 500 mL IV bag running at 50 mL per hour. After 6 hours, how many mL remain?
choices: 100 mL
200 mL
250 mL
300 mL
teas.exp: Infused = 50 × 6 = 300 mL. Remaining = 500 − 300 = 200 mL.

teas.q: What is the basic unit of life?
choices: An organ
A cell
A tissue
A system
teas.exp: The cell is the smallest living unit. Groups of similar cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form systems.

teas.q: Which organ pumps blood throughout the body?
choices: Lungs
Liver
Heart
Kidneys
teas.exp: The heart is the muscular pump of the cardiovascular system. It beats about 60–100 times per minute at rest.

teas.q: What does the respiratory system do?
choices: Digests food
Brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide
Filters blood
Sends nerve signals
teas.exp: The lungs take in O₂ and expel CO₂. This gas exchange happens in tiny sacs called alveoli.

teas.q: Which system includes bones and joints?
choices: Muscular system
Skeletal system
Nervous system
Endocrine system
teas.exp: The skeletal system provides structure, protects organs, and works with muscles to allow movement. Adults have 206 bones.

teas.q: What is the primary function of the digestive system?
choices: To pump blood
To break down food and absorb nutrients
To control body temperature
To produce hormones
teas.exp: The digestive system (mouth → esophagus → stomach → intestines) breaks food into nutrients the body can absorb.

teas.q: The nervous system is made up of the brain, spinal cord, and ___.
choices: Lungs
Kidneys
Nerves
Muscles
teas.exp: Nerves carry electrical signals between the brain/spinal cord and the rest of the body.

teas.q: Which organ filters waste from the blood to produce urine?
choices: Liver
Stomach
Kidney
Spleen
teas.exp: The kidneys filter about 200 liters of blood per day. The urinary system includes the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra.

teas.q: Which of the following is a function of the integumentary system?
choices: Hormone secretion
Protection against infection and temperature regulation
Digestion of fats
Oxygen transport
teas.exp: The integumentary system (skin, hair, nails) acts as a barrier against pathogens and helps regulate body temperature through sweating.

teas.q: Arteries carry blood ___ the heart; veins carry blood ___ the heart.
choices: to / from
away from / to
through / around
into / out of
teas.exp: Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart to body tissues. Veins return deoxygenated blood back to the heart.

teas.q: The endocrine system communicates by releasing ___.
choices: Electrical signals
Hormones
Enzymes
Antibodies
teas.exp: The endocrine system uses hormones — chemical messengers released into the bloodstream — to regulate body functions like metabolism and blood sugar.

teas.q: Which type of muscle tissue is found in the heart?
choices: Skeletal
Smooth
Cardiac
Connective
teas.exp: Cardiac muscle is involuntary, striated, and found only in the heart. It contracts continuously without tiring.

teas.q: What is the role of red blood cells?
choices: Fighting infection
Transporting oxygen via hemoglobin
Clotting wounds
Producing antibodies
teas.exp: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) contain hemoglobin, an iron-rich protein that binds oxygen and carries it from the lungs to body tissues.

teas.q: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
choices: Cerebrum
Cerebellum
Brain stem
Hypothalamus
teas.exp: The cerebellum (back of the brain) coordinates voluntary movements and maintains balance. Damage can cause ataxia (unsteady gait).

teas.q: During cellular respiration, glucose is broken down to produce energy in the form of ___.
choices: DNA
ATP
RNA
Protein
teas.exp: Cellular respiration converts glucose + oxygen → ATP (adenosine triphosphate) + CO₂ + water. ATP is the cell's energy currency.

teas.q: A patient has a blockage in the left anterior descending (LAD) artery. Which part of the heart is most at risk?
choices: Right atrium
Left ventricle
Right ventricle
Sinoatrial node
teas.exp: The LAD supplies blood to the anterior (front) left ventricle and interventricular septum. Blockage causes a 'widowmaker' heart attack.

teas.q: DNA is found in which part of a cell?
choices: Cell membrane
Cytoplasm
Nucleus
Ribosome
teas.exp: The nucleus is the control center of the cell. It contains DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid), which carries genetic instructions.

teas.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of living things?
choices: Ability to grow
Made of cells
Ability to reproduce
Made of metal
teas.exp: Living things: made of cells, grow, reproduce, respond to stimuli, use energy, maintain homeostasis. Metal is not a characteristic of life.

teas.q: In photosynthesis, plants convert sunlight, water, and CO₂ into ___.
choices: Oxygen and nitrogen
Glucose and oxygen
ATP and CO₂
Protein and fat
teas.exp: Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + 6O₂. Plants produce oxygen as a byproduct.

teas.q: Which type of cell division produces sex cells (eggs and sperm)?
choices: Mitosis
Meiosis
Binary fission
Budding
teas.exp: Meiosis produces 4 haploid (half-chromosome) gametes. Mitosis produces 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair.

teas.q: A recessive trait will only appear in a person's phenotype when ___.
choices: One dominant allele is present
Two copies of the recessive allele are present
The person is female
The trait is on the Y chromosome
teas.exp: Recessive alleles (aa) are only expressed when no dominant allele (A) masks them. A person with Aa has the dominant phenotype but is a carrier.

teas.q: Which of the following best describes natural selection?
choices: Random changes in DNA that occur over time
Individuals with traits better suited to their environment survive and reproduce more
All members of a species change together in response to the environment
Traits acquired during a lifetime are passed to offspring
teas.exp: Darwin's natural selection: heritable variation exists → some variants improve survival → those individuals reproduce more → traits become more common.

teas.q: What is an atom?
choices: The smallest unit of an element
A type of molecule
A charged particle
A compound
teas.exp: An atom is the smallest unit of an element that retains its chemical properties. Atoms are made of protons, neutrons, and electrons.

teas.q: Water (H₂O) is a ___.
choices: Element
Compound
Mixture
Atom
teas.exp: A compound is a substance made of two or more elements chemically bonded. H₂O has 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom bonded together.

teas.q: Which of the following is a chemical change?
choices: Melting ice
Cutting paper
Burning wood

teas.q: An acid has a pH ___ 7; a base has a pH ___ 7.

less than / greater than
equal to / less than
equal to / greater than

teas.q: Newton's Second Law states that Force equals ___.
choices: mass × velocity
mass × acceleration
distance / time
weight × gravity
teas.exp: F = ma. Force (Newtons) = mass (kg) × acceleration (m/s²). Doubling mass while keeping acceleration constant doubles the force needed.

teas.q: In a scientific experiment, the variable that the researcher changes on purpose is called the ___ variable.
choices: Dependent
Independent
Controlled
Random
teas.exp: The independent variable is deliberately manipulated. The dependent variable is what changes in response. Controlled variables are kept constant.

teas.q: A hypothesis must be ___.
choices: Proven correct to be useful
Testable and falsifiable
Based on facts, not observations
Approved by a committee
teas.exp: A valid scientific hypothesis must be testable (you can design an experiment) and falsifiable (it could potentially be proven wrong).

teas.q: A researcher studies whether a new drug reduces blood pressure. Participants who receive a sugar pill instead of the drug are in the ___ group.
choices: Experimental
Control
Dependent
Variable
teas.exp: The control group receives no treatment (or placebo) and serves as a baseline for comparison with the experimental group.

teas.q: A study finds that ice cream sales and drowning rates both increase in summer. This is an example of ___.
choices: Causation
Correlation without causation
An experimental finding
Confirmation bias
teas.exp: Both are caused by a third variable (hot weather/summer). Correlation does not imply causation. Ice cream doesn't cause drowning.

teas.q: In the sentence 'The nurse quickly checked the patient's vital signs,' which word is an adverb?
choices: nurse
quickly
checked
patient's
teas.exp: An adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. 'Quickly' modifies the verb 'checked' — it tells HOW she checked.

teas.q: Which of the following is a noun?
choices: Run
Beautiful
Slowly
Hospital
teas.exp: Nouns name people, places, things, or ideas. 'Hospital' is a place. Run (verb), Beautiful (adjective), Slowly (adverb).

teas.q: Which word is a conjunction in this sentence? 'The doctor and the nurse discussed the treatment plan.'
choices: doctor
and
discussed
treatment
teas.exp: Conjunctions join words, phrases, or clauses. 'And' joins 'doctor' and 'nurse.' Other conjunctions: but, or, nor, for, yet, so (FANBOYS).

teas.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: The patients is waiting in the lobby.
The patients are waiting in the lobby.
The patients am waiting in the lobby.
The patients were wait in the lobby.
teas.exp: 'Patients' is a plural noun, so it requires the plural verb 'are.' Singular: 'The patient is waiting.'

teas.q: Select the correct verb: 'Neither the doctor nor the nurses ___ available.'
choices: is
are
was
were
teas.exp: With 'neither...nor' / 'either...or,' the verb agrees with the subject CLOSEST to it. Closest subject = 'nurses' (plural) → 'are.'

teas.q: Which sentence uses a comma correctly?
choices: She took the patient's blood pressure, and recorded it in the chart.
She took the patient's blood pressure and, recorded it in the chart.
She, took the patient's blood pressure and recorded it in the chart.
She took the patient's blood pressure and recorded it in the chart.
teas.exp: No comma needed before 'and' when connecting two verbs with the same subject ('She took... and recorded...'). A comma before 'and' is used to join two independent clauses.

teas.q: Which sentence correctly uses an apostrophe?
choices: The nurses station is on the third floor.
The nurse's station is on the third floor.
The nurses' station is on the third floor.
Both B and C are correct, depending on number of nurses.
teas.exp: B: one nurse owns it (nurse's). C: multiple nurses share it (nurses'). Both are grammatically correct depending on context.

teas.q: Which option correctly punctuates this sentence? 'The patient had three symptoms ___ fever, chills, and fatigue.'
choices: The patient had three symptoms, fever, chills, and fatigue.
The patient had three symptoms: fever, chills, and fatigue.
The patient had three symptoms; fever, chills, and fatigue.
The patient had three symptoms — fever, chills, and fatigue.
teas.exp: A colon introduces a list after an independent clause. Options A (comma) and C (semicolon) are incorrect here. Option D (em-dash) is informal but also acceptable; B is the standard.

teas.q: Which of the following is a complete sentence?
choices: Running down the hallway.
The CNA documented the vital signs.
When the patient arrived at the clinic.
Because the temperature was elevated.
teas.exp: A complete sentence needs a subject and a predicate (verb). B: Subject = 'CNA', verb = 'documented.' A, C, D are fragments — they lack a main clause.

teas.q: Which of the following is a run-on sentence?
choices: The patient was discharged, and she was given follow-up instructions.
The patient was discharged she was given follow-up instructions.
Although the patient was discharged, she needed follow-up care.
After discharge, the patient received follow-up instructions.
teas.exp: A run-on sentence joins two independent clauses without proper punctuation. B has two complete thoughts smashed together with no connector.

teas.q: Identify the error: 'Having finished the assessment, the chart was updated by the nurse.'
choices: Subject-verb disagreement
Dangling modifier
Run-on sentence
Incorrect punctuation
teas.exp: A dangling modifier: 'Having finished the assessment' modifies the wrong noun. The chart didn't finish the assessment — the nurse did. Correct: 'Having finished the assessment, the nurse updated the chart.'

teas.q: Which sentence uses the correct verb tense? The patient ___ her medication every morning for the past year.

teas.exp: 'For the past year' signals an action that started in the past and continues to the present → present perfect tense: 'has taken.'

had dressed
has dressed
dresses
teas.exp: Two past events: dressing the wound (earlier) and the doctor arriving (later). Earlier past action = past perfect: 'had dressed.'

teas.q: Choose the correct word pair: 'The effect of the medication will ___ the patient's pain.'

effect
affekt
effekt
teas.exp: 'Affect' is typically the verb (to influence). 'Effect' is typically the noun (the result). 'Will affect' = correct verb use.

teas.q: Which of the following is appropriate for a professional medical record?
choices: The patient was freaking out about the injection.
The patient expressed anxiety regarding the injection procedure.
Patient kinda didn't want to get the shot.
Patient was super nervous about the needle.
teas.exp: Medical documentation requires formal, objective, clinical language. Slang ('freaking out,' 'kinda,' 'super nervous') is inappropriate in professional records.

teas.q: Revise for professional tone: 'She fell out of bed because she's kinda clumsy and wasn't careful.'
choices: Patient fell due to carelessness.
Patient was found on the floor beside the bed; no witness to the fall.
The patient fell because she didn't hold on to the rail.
Patient fell. She is clumsy.
teas.exp: Documentation should be factual and objective — report what was observed, not what you assumed. B states the facts without judgment.
